stories.headline: Modi visits Gothenburg, Sweden and India elevate ties to Strategic Partnership
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Gothenburg on May 17–18 at PM Kristersson's invitation for bilateral talks, a joint session at the European Round Table for Industry alongside European Commission President von der Leyen, and meetings with Swedish and European CEOs. The two leaders announced an India-Sweden Strategic Partnership, adopted a Joint Action Plan 2026–2030 covering trade, defence, AI, green transition, and space, and pledged to double bilateral trade from $7.75 billion within five years. Modi also received Sweden's Royal Order of the Polar Star.

stories.headline: Riksbank holds rate at 1.75%, signals possible hike; IMF and banks weigh in
stories.summary: The Riksbank held its policy rate unchanged at 1.75% at its May 6 meeting, publishing minutes on May 13 that showed a unanimous board but with governor Thedéen explicitly warning that a rate hike draws nearer the longer Middle East supply disruptions persist. The IMF, concluding its 2026 Article IV visit on the same day, issued a statement endorsing the hold while flagging war-related risks to Sweden's recovery. Meanwhile, commercial banks' earlier unilateral mortgage rate hikes drew criticism from Thedéen and the finance minister; April CPI fell unexpectedly to -0.1%.

stories.headline: Malmer Stenergard leads Swedish push at EU FAC for Russia sanctions and Israel settler pressure
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Malmer Stenergard attended the EU Foreign Affairs Council in Brussels on May 11, where she called Russia 'not really interested in peace' and advocated for a 21st sanctions package, including a full ban on services to vessels leaving Russian ports. She also backed sanctions on extremist Israeli ministers and tariffs on settlement goods. The EU subsequently agreed to expand sanctions on Israeli settlers after Hungary dropped its veto.

stories.headline: Aurora 26: Ukrainian drone pilots expose major gaps in Swedish NATO-exercise defense
stories.summary: During the large-scale NATO exercise Aurora 26 on Gotland, Ukrainian drone pilot teams playing the role of the adversary 'destroyed' Swedish forces, with one pilot stating that if the scenario had been real 'they would have been dead.' Defense Minister Jonson acknowledged the outcome was 'demanding' and said Sweden must practice more with Ukraine. Former defense minister Peter Hultqvist called for urgent investment in drone capability.

stories.headline: Jonson at EU defence ministers meeting and B9 summit in Bucharest; advocates EU defence clause clarity
stories.summary: Defense Minister Pål Jonson attended the EU Foreign Affairs Council defence configuration in Brussels on May 12 and the B9 summit in Bucharest on May 13, telling journalists Ukraine's defence plan is 'working' and Russia 'significantly exhausted.' He argued for clarifying the EU's collective defence clause (Article 42.7) as a NATO complement, while rejecting Spain's proposal for a joint EU army. At B9, Nordic and eastern flank leaders signed a joint declaration labelling Russia the 'most significant and direct long-term threat' to NATO.

stories.headline: Sweden to host NATO foreign ministers meeting in Helsingborg; Rutte bilateral with Kristersson announced
stories.summary: Sweden will host the NATO foreign ministers meeting in Helsingborg on May 21–22. Ahead of it, Kristersson and Malmer Stenergard called a press briefing on May 18. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte will also make a bilateral visit to Kristersson on May 21 and tour Sweden's civil defence training centre in Revinge, with Jonson and the Civil Defence Minister also attending.

stories.headline: Moderaterna campaign bus tour through Skåne; Kristersson warns of left-wing tax rises ahead of autumn election
stories.summary: Kristersson and several Moderate ministers conducted a multi-day campaign bus tour through Skåne and southern Sweden starting May 11, visiting schools, industrial sites, and towns. Kristersson framed the autumn election as a choice between Moderate tax discipline and left-wing tax increases, while the party held its Sverigemöte in Stockholm. Commentary debated whether this would be Kristersson's last election as Moderate leader.

stories.headline: Kristersson nepotism controversy: Social Democrats demand external review over Teach for Sweden grants
stories.summary: Aftonbladet reported that a foundation (Teach for Sweden) whose board includes Kristersson's sister-in-law received a 12 million kronor funding increase in the spring amendment budget, and that Kristersson participated in the government decision. The Social Democrats called for an external conflict-of-interest review; Kristersson denied knowing of the grants. Media linked the case to broader patterns including his childhood friend appointed as national security adviser.

stories.headline: Swedish Armed Forces military expansion: satellites, F16 growth, coastal guard armament, new company council
stories.summary: Multiple developments this week showed Sweden's ongoing military build-up: the first military surveillance satellite began delivering images; the Swedish Air Force filed to massively expand operations at F16 in Uppsala from 4,300 to 29,300 annual flights; the Coast Guard is arming vessels against drone threats; the Armed Forces launched a new corporate advisory council (excluding Volvo Cars for security reasons); and plans for ten military satellites over two years were disclosed.

stories.headline: SÄPO arrests two suspects for supplying advanced technology to Russia
stories.summary: Sweden's security service SÄPO announced on May 11 that two people had been detained on suspicion of helping Russia procure advanced engineering products usable in its war against Ukraine. SÄPO conducted searches across Stockholm, southern, and western Sweden. A SÄPO official stated that 'the Russian war industry depends on technology, including from Sweden.'

stories.headline: Wallenberg family launches Nordic Compass pan-Nordic industrial alliance
stories.summary: Jacob Wallenberg joined the board of Nordic Compass, a new alliance of over 25 Nordic corporations including Ericsson, Nokia, Nordea, and EQT, launched to boost the competitiveness of Nordic industry. Wallenberg said the Nordics risk losing companies to the US, and described the initiative as a response to the need to better leverage shared industrial strengths. Separately, Wallenberg-owned Verkan AB confirmed plans for a gunpowder factory in Björneborg creating 450 jobs.

stories.headline: Åkesson's foreign policy shift draws criticism from SD's own former leaders
stories.summary: SD's former party leader Mikael Jansson (now AFS) told the far-right outlet Nya Tider that Åkesson 'may have been bought' given his support for Israel and the United States, representing a sharp change from SD's historical positions. Separately, a retrospective analysed how Åkesson's stance on teenage deportations shifted abruptly under media pressure, and left-wing commentators questioned his recently adopted Christian rhetoric.
